newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African truth body subpoenas ex-police chief.
newsitem.headline: S.African truth body subpoenas ex-police chief.

text.p: South Africa's "truth commission" said on Thursday it had ordered a fourth apartheid- era police general, Johan Coetzee, to appear for grilling over human rights abuses.

"(He) was served a subpoena (on Wednesday) night by the investigative unit of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. He is scheduled to appear before an investigative inquiry on October 30," a commission statement said.
The commission said the spate of subpoenas was prompted by the reluctance of apartheid-era operatives to approach it for amnesty and come clean about their past activities.

Coetzee, a former police commissioner, and the three others are scheduled to appear before the commission's investigative arm later this month, a commission spokeswoman said. All four would testify in camera.

Five former senior secret policemen, including Brigadier Jack Cronje who ran a notorious death-squad unit, have volunteered to give the commission information on a series of murders of anti-apartheid activists. They are expected to present formal amnesty applications on Monday.

The commission, chaired by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Bishop Desmond Tutu, was set up last year to probe human rights abuses during 30 years of apartheid rule. The commission has the power to grant amnesty to those who confess apartheid crimes.
